Andy Robertson, the Liverpool defender, has emphasized the importance of improving the team's defensive performance as they prepare for their first season under the new manager, Arne Slot. The early signs have been promising, with Liverpool keeping two clean sheets in their opening two matches. However, they face a more significant test on Sunday when they travel to Manchester United.

Handle the defensive challenges Liverpool faced last season, Robertson acknowledged that the club conceded more goals than the eventual champions, Manchester City, and the runners-up, Arsenal. This was a contributing factor in their inability to maintain their title challenge. The defender believes that by limiting the number of chances their opponents create, Liverpool can avoid being "punished" in crucial games, as happened last season.

Robertson's comments suggest that Slot's priority in his first season at the helm will be to shore up the team's defensive record. The early clean sheets against Ipswich and Brentford have provided a solid foundation, but the United match will be a crucial test of their progress. Liverpool's ability to limit the opportunities for their opponents, particularly the in-form Manchester United attack, will be a key factor in determining their chances of mounting a successful title challenge in the upcoming season.
